assessment.title: Homework #6 · BJT operating regions and DC bias
assessment.topic: Module 6 · BJT · Junction-bias test · DC bias · PNP · Push-pull
assessment.instructions: Unless stated otherwise: silicon BJT, V_BE ≈ 0.7 V in forward-active, V_CE(sat) ≈ 0.2 V, V_BE(sat) ≈ 0.8 V, and neglect leakage currents. Show the assumed region, solve, and verify it with V_CE (V_EC) and the junction biases. Enter numbers in the units shown.

questions.title: 1) npn operating region from terminal voltages
questions.promptHtml:
For each case, identify the operating region (cutoff / forward-active / saturation) of an npn BJT and justify it with the EB/CB junction bias test.

  1. VB = 1.0 V, VE = 0 V, VC = 5.0 V
  2. VB = 0.2 V, VE = 0 V, VC = 5.0 V
  3. VB = 1.0 V, VE = 0.4 V, VC = 0.3 V
hints: Compute V_BE and V_BC for each case.
EBJ forward (V_BE ≳ 0.5 V) and CBJ reverse → forward-active; both forward → saturation; EBJ off → cutoff.

questions.title: 2) npn bias with R_B and R_E (β = 80)
questions.promptHtml:
VCC = +10 V, RC = 2.2 kΩ, VBB = +3.0 V, RB = 220 kΩ, RE = 680 Ω, β = 80.

  1. Assume forward-active; solve for IB, IC, IE and VB, VE, VC.
  2. Check whether the assumption is valid (VCE and junction bias).
  3. If invalid, re-solve in saturation using VCE(sat) and VBE(sat).
hints: Base-emitter loop: V_BB = I_B R_B + 0.7 + (β + 1)I_B R_E.
Valid if V_CE > V_CE(sat) and the CBJ is reverse biased.
checklist: Find all currents and node voltages.

responseFields.label: Validity check (and whether step 3 is needed)

questions.title: 5) Complementary emitter follower at DC
questions.promptHtml:
Q1 (npn) has its collector at +5 V; Q2 (pnp) has its collector at −5 V. The bases are tied together and driven from +5 V through RB = 47 kΩ. The emitters are tied together at the output vo, and RL = 4.7 kΩ connects vo to ground. VBE ≈ 0.7 V when ON, β = 100 for both.

  1. Which transistor conducts at DC?
  2. Find vo, the base voltage vB, the load current iL, and the base current iB.
hints: The base is pulled up toward +5 V, so v_B > v_o: which emitter junction is forward biased?
checklist: Check the ON device is not saturated and the OFF device's junction is reverse biased.

questions.promptHtml:
Circuit Studio problem · Breadboard twin, multimeter and Fault Challenge. Simulation tools are switched on for this question. Record each prediction before you use the tool that checks it.

The network of Problem 3 with RC = 2.2 kΩ: VCC = 15 V, RB1 = 120 kΩ (top), RB2 = 60 kΩ (bottom), RC = 2.2 kΩ, RE = 1 kΩ, β = 150.

  1. Predict: with VBE = 0.7 V and the Thevenin equivalent of the divider, find IC.
  2. Open Edit circuit → Breadboard. Build the circuit yourself from the This circuit parts bin; do not use Build for me. Mind the transistor's E–B–C pin order, and use Inside strips (X-Ray) if a node will not complete. Continue until every node is complete.
  3. Switch Power ON and use the multimeter to measure VB, VE and VC to ground. Compute IC ≈ VE/RE.
  4. Back on the schematic, change β to 50 and then 300 (in the Solution tab, under the circuit values and BJT model) and record IC each time.
  5. Return to the breadboard, open Lab Mystery · Fault Challenge in the Breadboard tools, and click Insert hidden fault (type Random mystery). Find the fault with the multimeter and record your measurements.
  6. Explain: why your measured IC is a little below the 0.7 V prediction, and why IC still changes noticeably with β, using RTH/(β + 1) compared with RE.
hints: V_TH = 15·60/180 V and R_TH = 120 kΩ ∥ 60 kΩ.
An open or wrong resistor shows up first as a node voltage far from your prediction.
checklist: Board built by hand; all nodes complete.
V_B, V_E, V_C measured with power on.
β sweep recorded; fault found with measurements.
